title: 1951 AHSME Problem 38
statement: A rise of \(600\) feet is required to get a railroad line over a mountain. The grade can be kept down by lengthening the track and curving it around the mountain peak. The additional length of track required to reduce the grade from \(3\%\) to \(2\%\) is approximately:

solutions.text:
A \(3\%\) grade requires about \(\frac{600}{0.03}=20{,}000\) feet of track, while a \(2\%\) grade requires \(\frac{600}{0.02}=30{,}000\) feet. The additional length is \(10{,}000\) feet.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Grade is rise divided by track length
